summary:
I've spent the last stretch on the GPU plumbing behind my local AI setup. Several models share one 16 GB Tesla P100, so Switchboard sits in front as a proxy that decides who gets the card. A request for one model evicts whichever model is loaded, waits for VRAM to settle, then streams the response. ComfyUI renders can't hold a lock, since they run asynchronously. So a custom node leases the GPU and releases it when the queue drains. The trap I found: if anything else grabs a lease under a different name, the broker evicts ComfyUI itself. Its coordinator then blocks inside its own event loop, and the whole server goes dark until the lease times out. I also added a long-context endpoint that fits a full 256K window by compressing the KV cache.

On The Long Rest, my D&D campaign manager, I mostly shipped things around a Foundry VTT module. The module pulls a session package into Foundry and pushes dice rolls and reveals back. The bug I enjoyed most: Foundry mutates the objects you hand to its create calls, deleting undefined fields in place. My reveal poller was reading its own inputs after the create and silently losing keys. It looked like a hung call until I traced it. Separately, I fixed a leak where the campaign endpoint returned entire database rows to every member. Those rows included encrypted provider keys and everyone's emails. It now uses explicit selects, and tests scan the serialized JSON for secret keys.

Also on The Long Rest, I added a character relationships feature: org charts and family trees that stay DM-only unless both ends are visible to players. For prep I built an importer that derives a campaign's notes, NPCs and beats from an adventure you paste in. It deliberately never stores the source text.

On the Hermes-Agent side, one fix was worth the time. The agent kept writing its own scripts instead of using its tools. The model wasn't disobeying. A circuit breaker was counting a tool's 404s as server failures, then telling the model to "use alternative approaches."

highlights.oneLiner: Proxy that decides which model gets the P100; found the ComfyUI lease deadlock.
Circuit breaker was counting 404s as outages, so the agent kept writing scripts.
Renders lease the GPU through a custom node and release when the queue drains.
